Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 35-year-old male with 3–6 month history of low mood, fatigue, anorexia, ~6 kg weight loss, episodic palpitations/subjective breathlessness in elevators, and history of untreated hypothyroidism.  
• Primary considerations (consistent with DDx):  
  – Major depressive disorder with somatic symptoms.  
  – Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism after stopping levothyroxine.  
  – Possible anaemia or other metabolic cause (vitamin deficiency, renal/hepatic dysfunction).  
  – Situational anxiety/panic contributing to elevator episodes.  
• No red-flag GI or respiratory symptoms; no exertional chest pain or dyspnoea.  
• Plan: order comprehensive blood panel; reassess results and consider need for physical examination, thyroid replacement, mental health support, or cardiology evaluation depending on findings.  
• Safety-netting: attend ED for chest pain, significant palpitations, new GI bleeding, persistent vomiting, or rapid clinical deterioration.  

Management Plan
- Arrange blood tests: CBC, U&E, LFTs, thyroid profile, vitamin levels, iron studies.  
- Patient instructed to contact support line to schedule phlebotomy; clinician to submit electronic request form.  
- Follow-up: patient will receive text to book review appointment once results available; advised to seek earlier review if symptoms worsen.  
- Education: discussed potential link between stopped thyroxine and symptoms; explained emergency indicators.  
- No medications started pending results.  

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above: planned  
- EPC referral for allied health (10x visits/year): not recorded  
- Dental referral: not recorded  
- Optometry referral: not recorded  
- Audiometry referral: not recorded  
- Dietitian referral: not recorded  
- CTG registration (if not enrolled): not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Major depressive disorder – High likelihood: low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss temporally related to job stress.  
2. Relapsed hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: known condition, stopped therapy, classic fatigue/low mood; weight loss atypical but possible appetite effect.  
3. Iron-deficiency or other anaemia – Moderate likelihood: fatigue, headaches; evaluation pending blood work.
